newsitem.title: UK: Saddam's son shot to avenge Iraqi general - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's son shot to avenge Iraqi general - paper.

text.p: A British newspaper said on Thursday that the attempted assassination of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's son Uday was part of a feud with the family of an Iraqi general killed by Saddam for criticising the government,
The Independent said it had learned from an Iraqi source that the leader of the plot was Ra'ad al-Hazaa, a former army officer in his thirties, who is the nephew of General Omar al-Hazaa.
The general, a member of the same Tikriti clan as Saddam, was executed in 1990.
The attempt to kill Uday, 32, took place as he drove through the Iraqi capital Baghdad on December 12.
Opposition groups say he was hit by four bullets, one of which is still lodged in his spine. The French government has turned down a request for him to be treated in France.
The request implies that Uday's wounds are serious, the Independent said.
The paper said the attack was previously claimed by al-Dawa, a militant Shia group with a history of trying to assassinate Iraqi leaders.

They are believed to have been involved in the logistics and organisation of the plot, but the driving force was Ra'ad Al-Hazaa and some of his relations, who were able to acquire details of Uday's movements because they moved in the same elite circles, the Independent said.
The feud which led to the attack on Uday had its origin in the killing of General Hazaa seven years ago, the paper said.
He retired during the war with Iran in the 1980s and became increasingly critical of Saddam. Arrested in 1990 he was executed, reputedly after his tongue was cut out, the Independent said.

An Iraqi army general now in exile was quoted as saying: "In 1990 the general was arrested. He was taken to al-Ouja and his tongue was cut out. Then he was executed. His son Farouq was killed at the same time and the general's house in Baghdad was bulldozed."
Uday is not known to have played any part in his death, but he is the most visible member of the regime in Baghdad.
The would-be assassins are said to have received information from "Lubna", a girlfriend of Uday, whose fate is unclear.
After the attack, the plotters fled to Iran, which has denied their presence in the country, the Independent said.
